title: Inference Metrics Exchange Hub: converged OTLP -> Prometheus + KPI enrichment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, tenant-sharded metrics exchange hub that normalizes incoming OTLP metric streams from inference nodes and edge proxies, enriches them with inference-specific KPIs (per-model latency buckets, batch size histograms, kv-cache hit labels, cost attribution tags), and exports Prometheus-compatible remote write shards for downstream scrapers. The hub should perform schema validation, label canonicalization, exemplar forwarding for trace linkability, adaptive high-cardinality reduction, and backpressure handling to protect Prometheus remote-write ingestion and long-term storage. This task implements the core transformation + routing layer and a short rollout plan for canary tenants.
acceptance_criteria: OTLP spans/metrics from test inference cluster are accepted and normalized into the exchange schema
Per-request latency_histogram and batch_size_histogram metrics are emitted with canonical labels: model, deployment, region, tenant_id
Exemplars are attached to latency histogram buckets with trace_id and request_id to support trace-linking dashboards
Prometheus remote_write output is tenant-sharded and can be routed to existing long-term storage clusters without label collisions
Backpressure: when downstream RW fails, exchange drains to a bounded local buffer and exposes a health/metric that triggers autoscaling
End-to-end tests validate that at 10k req/s anecdotal load, cardinality reduction keeps series ingestable (< 200k series) for our RU tenants

notes: Trade-offs discussed: doing heavy label normalization in the hub reduces downstream cardinality but increases CPU cost at the edge; decided to centralize canonicalization to limit schema drift.
We intentionally decoupled trace ingestion; exemplars contain only trace_id + request_id and a small set of context labels to avoid PII in metrics path.
Rollout strategy: start with 3 low-volume internal tenants + synthetic load, monitor series count & RW error rates, then widen to RU customers if stable.
